question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{coth}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

First, we recall the following  identities:

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x},\,\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral using the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{coth}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-\operatorname{sinh}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{3-{3}^{-1}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{8}{3})}{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{6} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
